kaps_punt: Geen inhoudstrepie. Hierdie les lewer KABV Afdeling 2.4.4 se konsep 'Historiese bronne en getuienis' en die 2.4.3-doelwit 'Die vind van 'n verskeidenheid soorte inligting oor die verlede', wat die inhoudstabel se opdrag oor Afdeling 2 vir elke inhoudsonderwerp vereis.

items.bewering: Die verlede is verby, en ons kan dit nie weer gaan bekyk nie. Tog weet ons vandag baie oor mense van lank gelede.
items.bron: History Skills, 'The difference between history and the past' (historyskills.com/2020/12/10/the-difference-between-history-and-the-past): the past is everything that happened before now and survives only in fragments; KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.4 (bl. 11). Volledige kontrole, eerste rondte.

items.bewering: Mense laat dinge agter wat lank na hulle tyd nog daar is. 'n Ou foto bly oor, en 'n ou pot bly in die grond.
items.bron: Pottery survives in the ground for thousands of years, and potsherds are among the most common finds on archaeological sites: Ministry Magazine, 'Pottery - A Boon to Archeologists' (1984), and the Tooley's Boatyard archaeology page 'What Pottery Reveals About Britain's Past'. That photographs are visual sources: KABV SW Gr 4 Kwartaal 1 (bl. 34), 'inligting vanaf foto's'.

items.bewering: Uit sulke dinge werk ons uit wat lank gelede gebeur het.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.4 (bl. 11): history is 'die interpretasie en verduideliking van inligting uit verskeie bronne'; UC Berkeley History-Social Science Project (ucbhssp.berkeley.edu/node/58): historians turn traces of the past into evidence.

items.bewering: 'n Leidraad is iets uit die verlede wat oorgebly het. Dit help ons om 'n vraag oor lank gelede te beantwoord.
items.bron: 'Leidraad' means 'clue' in Afrikaans: Global Symbols / Blissymbolics, entry 'clue' (Afrikaans: leidraad). Do not take the Dutch meaning ('guideline', 'handbook') as the meaning here. A trace of the past that answers a question: UC Berkeley HSSP (ucbhssp.berkeley.edu/node/58). Memories and stories handed down count as something that 'remains' (oorgebly), so the definition also covers the oral group in the same block.

items.bewering: Wanneer ons dit so gebruik, word dit 'n bewys.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.4 (bl. 11): 'Bewyse word geskep wanneer die bronne wat gebruik word om die vrae oor die verlede te beantwoord.' Also the NSW Curriculum glossary 'source' (a source is used to elicit evidence to answer a historical question); SCSA Western Australia glossary 'source' (a source becomes evidence if it is of value to an inquiry); Collingwood as quoted in Partisan Review 1994 ('nothing is evidence except in relation to some definite question'). 'Bewys' is CAPS's own Afrikaans term for evidence.

items.bewering: Ons noem al hierdie leidrade uit die verlede ook bronne.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4 Kwartaal 1, Agtergrondsinligting (bl. 34): the word 'bronne' stands for 'hoe vind ons inligting oor die verlede'. Afdeling 2.4.4 'Historiese bronne en getuienis'. The sentence says that clues are called sources, not that every source is a clue, so secondary sources do not make it false.

items.bewering: Ons deel die leidrade in verskillende groepe in. Vier van daardie groepe is visuele, mondelinge en geskrewe leidrade, en voorwerpbronne.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4 Kwartaal 1 (bl. 34): information from photos, writings, stories and interviews with people, and objects, which are the same four groups; Afdeling 2.4.3 (bl. 10) names visual material, interviews and written information. Internationally the same four-way split (written, visual, oral, artefacts) is standard in primary history: the Historical Association, 'What's important about... Sources and evidence' (history.org.uk/primary/resource/10764); Durham University 4Schools history resources. The wording 'Vier van daardie groepe' leaves room for other groups, which is correct.

items.bewering: Dink aan 'n speurder wat 'n ou raaisel moet oplos. Sy was self nie daar toe dit gebeur het nie. Sy soek leidrade en gebruik bewyse om uit te vind wat gebeur het. 'n Geskiedkundige soek ook leidrade en gebruik bewyse om 'n antwoord uit te werk.
items.bron: The historian-as-detective comparison is an established one: Robin Winks (ed.), 'The Historian as Detective: Essays on Evidence' (Harper & Row, 1968/69), catalogue entry at lib.ecu.edu/catalog-preview/catalog/4459; Partisan Review 61(4) 1994, p. 667 (bu.edu), which traces it to John Dickson Carr (1931) and Collingwood. On the mapping: absence from the event, clues and evidence all map correctly, and a detective who questions witnesses maps onto oral sources. The obvious place it breaks, that a detective reaches one definite solution while history often does not, is closed by the lesson itself in the same block ('Twee geskiedkundiges kan dieselfde leidrade anders lees') and in 'Wat geskiedenis is' ('die vraag bly oop'). Winks's own reviewers name exactly this difference (the historian is not bound to an either-or answer), so the lesson's correction is the right one. A learner who reasons further from the comparison is not led astray.

items.bewering: Twee geskiedkundiges kan dieselfde leidrade anders lees.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.3 (bl. 10): 'Verduidelik waarom die gebeure in die verlede dikwels verskillend geinterpreteer word'; Afdeling 2.4.4 'Multi-perspektief benadering' (bl. 11), on the different ways historians have written about the past.

items.bewering: By 'n ou pot sien die een roet en dink dit was 'n kookpot.
items.bron: Exterior soot is a standard archaeological indicator of use over a fire and of cooking: Skibo, 'Pottery Function: A Use-Alteration Perspective' (Springer, 1992); Skibo, Kalinga dissertation (repository.arizona.edu/handle/10150/185281), where carbon deposits are linked to observed cooking; Radiocarbon, 'Food and soot organic residues on outer pottery surfaces' (Cambridge, 2017). The lesson presents this as one historian's interpretation, not as fact, which is correct: soot shows use over a fire, and cooking is the obvious but not the only reading.

items.bewering: Die ander sien die smal opening en dink dit was 'n waterpot.
items.bron: Narrow-necked vessels are generally interpreted as containers for liquids, because the opening limits spilling and evaporation: Jewish Museum, storage jar catalogue entries (collections.thejewishmuseum.org); Qatar Museums, transport jar from Murwab ('oil, water, wine or syrup'). A Southern African anchor: University of the Free State, 'Some clay vessels formerly used by the South Sotho' (scholar.ufs.ac.za), where the nkho is a narrow-necked pot for carrying water and storing liquids; Royal Museum for Central Africa, Comparative Bantu Pottery Vocabulary (S33, nkho: pot to carry and store water). The sources note that a narrow neck sometimes also served dry goods, so this too is correctly presented as one historian's interpretation.

The pot example as a whole: both readings rest on real, recognised archaeological indicators (soot gives use over a fire; a narrow neck gives storage of liquids, per the sources above), so the example shows correctly how one source supports two defensible interpretations. The mapping holds. Nothing in it invites a learner to conclude that one of the two must be wrong.

items.bewering: 'n Geskiedkundige vind uit hoe mense vroeër geleef het. Sy vind uit wat die belangrike gebeurtenisse was en hoekom dinge gebeur het.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.1 (bl. 9): 'Wat het gebeur? Wanneer het dit gebeur? Waarom het dit dan gebeur?'; Afdeling 2.4.4 'Oorsaak en gevolg' (bl. 11).

items.bewering: Geskiedenis is die studie van die verlede: wat ons vanuit bronne kan uitvind oor hoe mense se lewe met die tyd verander en ontwikkel het.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.1 (bl. 9): 'Geskiedenis is die studie van verandering en ontwikkeling, in die samelewing oor 'n tydperk.' Afdeling 2.4.4 (bl. 11): history is the interpretation of information from sources. The lesson combines the two faithfully.

items.bewering: Dit is nie die verlede self nie, maar wat ons uit die leidrade uitwerk.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.4 (bl. 11): 'Geskiedenis is nie "die verlede" self nie. Dit is die interpretasie en verduideliking van inligting uit verskeie bronne.' Also Ruth Sandwell, 'History vs. the Past' (canadianmysteries.ca/en/3515.html), and History Skills (historyskills.com).

items.bewering: Soms wys hulle nie genoeg nie en die vraag bly oop.
items.bron: The surviving evidence is incomplete, so some historical questions remain unresolved: Canadian Mysteries, 'History vs. the Past'; Mathematical Association of America essay on history and evidence (maa.org); and Winks (1968) as summarised on Goodreads (evidence is incomplete and can be revised).

items.bewering: geskiedkundige: Iemand wat uit leidrade uitwerk wat lank gelede gebeur het en hoe mense toe geleef het.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.1 and 2.4.4 (bl. 9 and 11); UC Berkeley HSSP. 'Lank gelede' simplifies, since historians also study the recent past, but the definition does not say 'only lank gelede', so it does not cross into falsehood. It agrees with the study text.

items.bewering: leidraad: Iets wat uit die verlede oorgebly het en 'n vraag help beantwoord.
items.bron: Same as the study-text sentence in 'Wat 'n leidraad is': Global Symbols (leidraad = clue); UC Berkeley HSSP (traces of the past turned into evidence by questions). Read on its own, the entry is still true.

items.bewering: bewys: 'n Bron of leidraad wat ons gebruik om 'n vraag oor die verlede te help beantwoord.
items.bron: KABV SW Gr 4-6, Afdeling 2.4.4 (bl. 11): evidence is created when sources are used to answer questions about the past; NSW Curriculum glossary 'source'; SCSA WA glossary 'source'; Collingwood (Partisan Review 1994). The entry deliberately says 'help beantwoord' rather than 'proves', and it is read alone, so it does not suggest certainty.

opsomming: Al 19 beweringe is teen bronne bevestig (KABV Afdeling 2.4 en Gr 4 Kwartaal 1, plus argeologiese en geskiedkundige bronne op die web); die les bevat geen superlatiewe nie, en albei vergelykings - die speurder en die ou pot - is op hul afbeelding nagegaan en hou, omdat die les self die plek toemaak waar die speurdervergelyking sou breek (een vaste antwoord teenoor 'n oop vraag).
